name: Anti-de Sitter Soliton
description: A smooth spacetime of negative energy with no horizon: the planar black hole of anti-de Sitter space with its time and one flat direction exchanged, so that the horizon becomes a tip where a circle shrinks to a point. Gary Horowitz and Robert Myers found it in 1998 and conjectured that it is the ground state of its boundary conditions.
convention: The anti-de Sitter radius $L$ is a length. We keep factors of $c$ explicit.
history: Can a spacetime weigh less than empty space? For one that approaches anti-de Sitter space in every direction the answer is no: its energy is well defined and can never be negative [abbott1982, gibbons1983, horowitz1998]. Wind one direction of space into a circle that shrinks to a point somewhere inside, and those proofs no longer apply [horowitz1998]. In flat space the news was already grim: the Kaluza-Klein vacuum, Edward Witten had found in 1982, is unstable, and in 1991 Dieter Brill and Gary Horowitz built smooth solutions with such a circle whose energy is as negative as one likes [witten1982kk, brill1991, horowitz1998].¶The circle mattered in 1998 because Witten wanted ordinary gluons out of a supersymmetric theory [witten1998thermal]. His recipe was to put the gauge theory on a circle around which the fermions change sign, which breaks supersymmetry and leaves the gauge fields as the only light degrees of freedom [witten1998thermal, horowitz1998]. In the dual gravity theory that circle sits at the boundary of a spacetime that looks like anti-de Sitter space only locally, the very setting in which no theorem guaranteed a lowest energy [horowitz1998]. So is the gauge theory unstable, or does the correspondence fail?¶That August Horowitz and Robert Myers found a third possibility [horowitz1998]. They took the planar black hole of anti-de Sitter space, exchanged its time with one of its flat directions, $t \to i\tau$ and $x \to it$, and wrote down $$ds^2 = \frac{r^2}{L^2}\left[-c^2dt^2 + \left(1 - \frac{r_0^{p+1}}{r^{p+1}}\right)d\tau^2 + dx^i dx^i\right] + \frac{L^2}{r^2}\left(1 - \frac{r_0^{p+1}}{r^{p+1}}\right)^{-1}dr^2$$ in $p + 2$ dimensions [horowitz1998]. The black hole's horizon becomes a tip at $r = r_0$ where the circle $\tau$ shrinks to a point, as smooth as the origin of a plane provided $\tau$ has the period $\beta = 4\pi L^2/((p + 1)r_0)$ [horowitz1998]. The result has no horizon and no singularity, and Horowitz and Myers named it the AdS soliton [horowitz1998].¶Its energy is negative: measured against anti-de Sitter space with the same circle, it is proportional to $-1/\beta^p$ [horowitz1998]. For the gauge theory this is welcome news, since fields on a circle that breaks supersymmetry carry a negative Casimir energy, and for $p = 3$ the two energies depend on every parameter in the same way and differ by a factor of $3/4$ [horowitz1998]. The same $3/4$ separates the entropy of a black brane with three spatial dimensions from that of the weakly coupled gauge theory, and Horowitz and Myers traced both to one Euclidean calculation [gubser1996, horowitz1998]. The factor relates the full stress tensors of the two descriptions as well [horowitz1998, myers1999]. In three dimensions, $p = 1$, the construction returns anti-de Sitter space itself, which lies below the BTZ black hole of zero mass [horowitz1998, banados1992].¶A stable gauge theory needs a ground state, so the soliton had to be the lightest spacetime with its boundary conditions, and Horowitz and Myers put that forward as a new positive energy conjecture [horowitz1998]. They admitted that "at first sight, this seems very unlikely", since the soliton has no constant curvature, no supersymmetry, "or any other distinguishing property" of the minimum energy solutions known before [horowitz1998]. Small perturbations raise its energy for $p = 3$, as they checked, and Neil Constable and Myers extended the check to every dimension in 1999 [horowitz1998, constable1999]. Gregory Galloway, Sumati Surya, and Eric Woolgar proved a uniqueness theorem for it among static spacetimes with a negative cosmological constant [galloway2002, galloway2003]. The conjecture itself held out, and as late as 2017 Woolgar could write that it "remains unproved, having so far resisted standard techniques" [woolgar2017].¶For metrics that are warped products over a half line the conjecture was verified in 2020 by Hamed Barzegar, Piotr Chruściel, Michael Hörzinger, Maciej Maliborski, and Luc Nguyen [barzegar2020, brendle2024]. Four years later Simon Brendle and Pei-Ken Hung proved a positive energy theorem for a moment of time symmetry in spacetimes of four to eight dimensions, with equality attained by Horowitz and Myers's metrics [brendle2024]. Sumati Surya, Kristin Schleich, and Donald Witt had by then taken the soliton as the ground state of the flat black holes, and found a phase transition between the two that the correspondence relates to confinement and deconfinement in the gauge theory [surya2001]. In the hands of Tatsuma Nishioka, Shinsei Ryu, and Tadashi Takayanagi its form in five dimensions became the insulator of a holographic transition from insulator to superconductor [nishioka2010].

related.text: The flat black hole of anti-de Sitter space, the black brane. Exchange its time with one flat direction and its horizon becomes the soliton's tip [horowitz1998].

At $r_0 = 0$ the line element is anti-de Sitter space's in its Poincaré patch, against which the soliton's negative energy is measured. In three dimensions the soliton is anti-de Sitter space itself [horowitz1998].

The black hole of three dimensions. Without rotation, and with its time and its angle exchanged, it is the soliton of three dimensions, which is anti-de Sitter space with no points identified [horowitz1998].

The round black hole of anti-de Sitter space, which trades places with anti-de Sitter space in Hawking and Page's phase transition. The flat black hole does the same with the soliton [hawking1983, surya2001].
The same exchange of time and a circle in flat space of five dimensions, where the bubble needs magnetic flux to give it mass and hold it open [bah2021].

coordinates.name: Horowitz-Myers

parameters.description: Radius of the tip, a length, where the circle $\tau$ shrinks to a point
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use Horowitz and Myers's coordinates $(t, r, \tau, x)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\tau$ and $x$ lengths, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The circle $\tau$ has period $\beta = 4\pi L^2/(3r_0)$, which makes the tip $r = r_0$ a regular point.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{r^3 - r_0^3}{L^4}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{2r^3 + r_0^3}{2r\left(r^3 - r_0^3\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{\left(2r^3 + r_0^3\right)\left(r^3 - r_0^3\right)}{2L^4\,r^3}\dot{\tau}^2 - \dfrac{r^3 - r_0^3}{L^4}\dot{x}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Poincaré

parameters.description: Tip, a length, $z_0 = L^2/r_0$, where the circle $\tau$ shrinks to a point
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, z, \tau, x)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\tau$ and $x$ lengths, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The length $z = L^2/r$, with $r$ the radius of Horowitz and Myers's chart and $r_0$ its value at the tip, vanishes on the conformal boundary. The circle $\tau$ has period $\beta = 4\pi z_0/3$.

coordinates.name: Polar

parameters.description: Radius of the tip in Horowitz and Myers's chart, a length, which sets the scale of $t$ and $x$
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \rho, \phi, x)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $x$ a length, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The proper distance $\rho$ from the tip is set by $r^3 = r_0^3\cosh^2(3\rho/2L)$, with $r$ the radius of Horowitz and Myers's chart, and $\phi = 2\pi\tau/\beta$ is the angle around the circle $\tau$ of period $\beta = 4\pi L^2/(3r_0)$.

coordinates.name: Five Dimensions

parameters.description: Radius of the tip, a length, where the circle $\tau$ shrinks to a point
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -6/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use Horowitz and Myers's coordinates $(t, r, \tau, x, y)$ in five dimensions, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\tau$, $x$, and $y$ lengths, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The circle $\tau$ has period $\beta = \pi L^2/r_0$, which makes the tip $r = r_0$ a regular point.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{r^4 - r_0^4}{L^4\,r}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{r^4 + r_0^4}{r\left(r^4 - r_0^4\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^4 + r_0^4\right)\left(r^4 - r_0^4\right)}{L^4\,r^5}\dot{\tau}^2 - \dfrac{r^4 - r_0^4}{L^4\,r}\dot{x}^2 - \dfrac{r^4 - r_0^4}{L^4\,r}\dot{y}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Three Dimensions

parameters.description: Radius of the tip, a length, where the circle $\tau$ shrinks to a point
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -1/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use Horowitz and Myers's coordinates $(t, r, \tau)$ in three dimensions, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\tau$ a length, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The circle $\tau$ has period $\beta = 2\pi L^2/r_0$, which makes the tip $r = r_0$ a regular point.
